scope: Observed controller submission/ACK/first-launch chain; no DMA wall anchor, exposed-stall measurement or counterfactual speedup.

prepare_host_lifetime.scope: Node/pool associations, not allocation continuity or model-forward reuse. A restore after observed Host eviction cannot establish consumption of the original prepared copy. Eviction latency stops at the next observed same-node/pool D2H write; absent eviction records are not zero evictions. Reported latencies include only observed evictions, excluding censored copies. Repeated context/epoch/node/creation identities are not exact duplicate bytes and do not establish the same wait episode across splits.

prepare_selection.scope: Candidate selection-time estimates, not reclaimed bytes, DMA bytes or forward-use credit. Zero direct reclaim may be a necessary ancestor backup before an exclusive checkpoint becomes reclaimable. Match ACKs by command ID only; legacy records without it remain unassociated. Missing candidate estimates remain unknown. For a burst, candidate transfer/reclaim estimates describe the selected first extent only; explicit burst IDs link additional per-node receipts without multiplying this estimate or granting reuse credit.

join_ticket.planning_gap_semantics: One count per independent wait per observed reason, regardless of repeated samples. Evidence categories partition waits; reason/detail groups overlap and must not be summed. Zero or missing plans do not prove zero physical demand. Residual bytes are next-request native FULL Host hits, not a proven pre-boundary opportunity, exclusive rejection cause or oracle speedup. Burst categories partition waits by the largest explicitly observed plan, not lifetime node commands. A sixteen-node plan is not proof of truncation or that a larger early transfer would fit capacity or the service window.

tool_wait.planning_gap_semantics: One count per independent wait per observed reason, regardless of repeated samples. Evidence categories partition waits; reason/detail groups overlap and must not be summed. Zero or missing plans do not prove zero physical demand. Residual bytes are next-request native FULL Host hits, not a proven pre-boundary opportunity, exclusive rejection cause or oracle speedup. Burst categories partition waits by the largest explicitly observed plan, not lifetime node commands. A sixteen-node plan is not proof of truncation or that a larger early transfer would fit capacity or the service window.

sibling_release_windows.semantics: Independent observed JOIN episodes, not all workload JOINs. Actual allocator release uses scheduler wall time; complete JOIN uses the existing client-clock offset conversion. Only explicitly identified dynamic subagents link by workflow/parent context/JOIN. Host-only or post-JOIN releases cannot support pre-JOIN H2D. A command qualifies only with the existing proof of actual pre-JOIN submission and FULL reuse by the following request. Temporal association does not prove exclusive capacity, child-to-parent page identity, that these bytes were necessary for prefetch, or a native-relative saving. Cumulative releases are not simultaneously free capacity; transferred FULL bytes are command receipts, not a count of unique pages. Unobserved JOIN completion leaves the release window unknown.

terminal_capacity_handoff.semantics: Actual terminal-suffix allocator release, linked to the first observed completed parent GPU batch, not kernel start; RETURN delivery observation and service observation use scheduler wall time, not client event time; not exclusive slot ownership, predictive H2D reuse, avoided D2H bytes, or a native-relative latency saving. Restore lookahead is selection evidence, not submission/ACK evidence. Aggregate releases include internal calls; scope breakdown and terminal_children use explicit invocation-create metadata or recorded runtime scope, never ID spelling. Only confirmed dynamic subagents link to JOIN parent services; absent metadata stays unknown. Missing pool byte sizes stay unknown.

parent_capacity_restore_retries.scope: linked child allocator release enables a demand retry; not pre-boundary H2D

source_summary_semantics: Per-source node commands, not independent requests or workflow events. FULL reuse counts include only commands with positive FULL transfer units. Pool bytes come from reconciled physical ACKs; missing legacy pool-byte evidence is reported, never reconstructed by byte shares. Execution handoff is submitted demand, separate from anticipatory JOIN/tool actions. FULL residency groups use the initial observed registration lock and last observed release reason in log order; absent evidence stays unknown. Groups are lifecycle associations, not isolated causes. Lease expiry does not imply a reuse miss, nor does registration prove continuous protection until service; Mamba-only transfers are excluded.
native_reload_attribution_semantics: Node/pool overlap before first service, not proof of repeated physical allocation or duplicate bytes. Mixed tagged batches retain untagged operations. Exact receipts carry per-operation units and bytes; legacy batch pool presence remains an ambiguous association. Evidence counts may overlap when a command has multiple reloads.
prepare_attribution_semantics: Latest observed D2H writer per node/pool. A later D2H is not proof of byte overwrite or duplicate transfer: Host eviction/reallocation, node splitting and legacy merged pool attribution are unresolved. Intervening same-node/pool Host eviction is reported when available; it does not recover an allocation identity across radix splits. The lifetime summary separates restore associations before/after observed Host eviction without changing legacy latest-writer association counts. Observed restoration is not final model-forward reuse.
wait_event_semantics: One causal JOIN per workflow/context/JOIN identity across parent epoch advances, or one tool wait at a context epoch, not one node command. JOIN service belongs to the first parent request after the observed complete JOIN, including plans logged after that request is submitted; an unobserved JOIN boundary leaves that request association unknown. Plans are bounded snapshots, not a continuous or counterfactual opportunity denominator; the maximum snapshot is not summed across repeated samples. Capacity conditions require observable exact FULL/Mamba free lists and a nonempty plan. An event may appear in multiple conditions at different snapshots; conditions do not prove unavailable cold victims, the cause of an actual rejection, or recoverable bytes after a policy change. Early FULL requires actual submit before complete JOIN/all-tool END and verified reuse by that episode's next request. Tool boundaries require the origin and following request plus every intervening tool, including sequential calls not active at the sampled plan. The following request is bound by the origin epoch, even if observation delivery occurs later. Sampled tool IDs outside that bounded request round are reported separately and cannot extend its completion boundary. Unclosed or unproven tool rounds keep their completion boundary unknown. Native Host-hit counters and exact demand handoff receipts are separate remaining-demand evidence; do not add them without proving disjoint allocations. Client-to-native-arrival includes request preparation, transport and serving frontend work, not an isolated client cost. HTTP hook timestamps separate client preparation from pool/transport and the body-sent-to-native-arrival interval, which still includes server ingress, validation, template/tokenization and IPC; it is not isolated tokenizer time. Ambiguous attempts, missing receipts and unordered boundaries keep the corresponding intervals unknown. Native-arrival-to-service wait includes admission and execution queueing, not isolated H2D delay. Sampled GPU dependency wait is a batch observation and must not be summed across its requests. FULL expiration stages locate observed locked-receipt releases relative to the causal boundary, client submit, native arrival and first service. They do not prove a reuse miss or an isolated cause; reuse evidence is reported separately. Missing or unordered boundaries remain unknown. Missing identities, clocks, ACK pool bytes or service evidence stay unknown.

shared_path_timing.clock: perf_counter_ns; CPU wall intervals, not GPU kernel time
shared_path_timing.scope: cumulative completed calls; exclusive totals avoid nested double counting

opportunity_writer_timing.scope: Every 64th record per category, starting with its first record. Measured processing samples only; queue waiting and status publication are excluded. Wall includes scheduling and GIL waiting; thread CPU excludes waiting. No full-run cost, GPU stall, GIL attribution or JCT saving is inferred.

prefix_semantics: Independent complete file prefixes capped at first-read stat sizes, with length and SHA256 verified on repeated reads. Not an atomic cross-file snapshot. Pending transfers and unobserved completion boundaries remain unknown. Handoff demand recovery is separate from pre-boundary prefetch.
